title: Naming squares fast, from either side
outcomes: Names a square pointed at on either side of the board without counting from the edge
Uses the square colour as a quick check on a name
Does not mirror squares when the board is turned

steps.text: In **The board and its square names** you learned that a square is its file letter, then its rank number. Now the aim is speed. Two habits replace counting. First, read the letter and number along the board's edge. Second, check the **colour** from the corner: a1 is dark, and colours alternate, so a square is dark when it is an even number of steps from a1 across and up added together (d4 is 3 across and 3 up, 6 steps, so dark). This holds on every square.

steps.caption: Naming squares by colour. The long line from a1 to h8 is all dark squares: a1, b2, c3, d4, e5, f6, g7, h8. Check d4: 3 steps across and 3 up from a1 is 6, even, so dark.

line.say: Now look at d4. It is dark, like a1: 3 steps across and 3 up is 6, even.

steps.text: Many boards and diagrams show letters and numbers, and many do not; this app's board can also be turned to Black's side. The skill is to name squares without needing the letters. The names stay with the squares, so only the picture changes. The common slip is to **mirror**: reading the square on screen as if White were looking, so b3 becomes g6. As a **rule of thumb**, find the letter on the edge first, then the number, and never copy the picture.

steps.title: One square, three ways of reading it
steps.prompt: The same white rook seen from White's side, seen from Black's side, and read by copying the picture as if White were looking. Predict first: which readings name the rook's square correctly?

steps.text: Limits of these checks. The colour test tells you a name is wrong, not which name is right: two dark squares both pass. It also cannot catch a board turned 180 degrees, because that keeps every square's colour, so use the corner check: a1 is dark at White's left, h1 is light at White's right. Both are **rules of thumb** for speed, so keep practising until naming is automatic.

steps.prompt: How sure are you that you can name any square pointed at, from either side, without counting? Which kind (a far corner, Black's side, a crowded middle) was slowest? (low / medium / high)
